claims.claim: Kennedy was assassinated November 22, 1963; the half-dollar act was approved December 30.
claims.media: Verified timeline graphic; not an image of the owner specimen.

claims.claim: Proof dies arrived January 2, regular production began January 30 in Denver and the following week in Philadelphia, and ceremonies took place February 11.
claims.media: Timeline; Mint facility images only after source and reuse rights review.

claims.claim: The 1964 half-dollar was 90 percent silver; 1965 composition changed to 40 percent amid a silver shortage.
claims.media: Source-matched composition comparison, clearly labeled by year; owner photo coin-0037 only as a general Kennedy design view after crop review.

claims.claim: The Mint’s engravers recalled selecting the half dollar in late November 1963. The Franklin half had not completed its statutory 25-year design period, so Congress passed legislation authorizing the new design.
claims.media: Dated legislative and denomination timeline; do not imply the owner photo coin is the 1964 issue.

claims.claim: Gilroy Roberts designed the obverse and Frank Gasparro the reverse; the Mint recollection describes adapting existing models during the accelerated project.
claims.media: Credit both designers and label recreated studio scenes as illustrations.

claims.claim: Jacqueline Kennedy suggested portrait adjustments on December 17, 1963; the revised design received approval on December 27, before the December 30 act.
claims.media: Timeline only; do not fabricate dialogue or portray a meeting as archival footage.

claims.claim: The Mint's recollection records an initial delivery of about 26 million Kennedy half dollars to the Federal Reserve on March 5, 1964.
claims.media: Use a labeled timeline or stack illustration, not the owner photo as proof of delivery or mintage.
